label: ACCOMPLISHED_COGNITIVE_CORRECTION_2: A change that actually replaces an erroneous judgment by a…
definition: A change that actually replaces an erroneous judgment by a correct one. No result in the explanation-order test asserts this stronger temporal claim.
note: Analyst contrast sense, attribution deferred. The shared temporal/error/correctness/withdrawal conditions are implemented in TruthCore.Logic.CognitiveReplacement.ReplacementConditions, but this is not yet a binding of the original sense. OPEN semantic scope: does replacement require the same subject revising the same matter, or may an explicit replacement link relate judgments on different matters? Same content cannot mean identical judgment: correction may reverse a verdict on that content. The common core uses actual endorsement at strictly ordered occasions, erroneous-before/correct-after under a supplied correctness norm, withdrawal of the old judgment, and an explicit replacement link. A later correct belief alone, retention of the erroneous endorsement, or a free replacement flag alone does not suffice. Correctness, actual-history applicability and the replacement link remain explicit semantic inputs; no report agreement, external warrant, factivity, authority or source instance follows. Keep CORRECTION_2 unresolved until the coordinator settles scope. The root connection plan is the existing reason/truth obligations via a separately justified genuine-moral-correction bridge (418606fa-bf33-5996-882e-5eebbe88ab22); neither that bridge nor need-to-accomplishment is asserted here. Explicit root-route target: STMT-RECOGNITION-ANSWERS-TO-SHARED-REASON (b025531d-6c4a-573a-a205-795fe8da514a). A future bridge would interpret a recognition revision as actual cognitive replacement and separately defend shared standards; this common core implies neither sharedness nor the correctness of any recognition. Applicability of this generic judgment history to recognition is the missing bridge, not a new result.
